text:
support-bot: ALERT from Support — ACME (Private VPC) reports intermittent 401s on hosted API and says there are no KMS audit events for their HSM-backed key (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd).

morgan.h: looping in eng-security. Customer says the problem started right after they applied a new iptables/firewall policy in their VPC. They have private control plane; customer-managed peering. Quick repro steps they sent:
  - from app pod: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -> returns 401
  - from their bastion host: same curl -> 200 OK
  - they claim KMS console shows no Decrypt events for that time range

samir.s: do we have control-plane auth logs showing token validation failures? If the control plane can't decrypt a customer token using their KMS key (external HSM), we'd see KMS.Decrypt errors. Ask Support for the full kube/insights logs and the exact time window. Also: did they rotate keys recently?

morgan.h: pasted customer logs (sanitized):
  "[2025-03-02T14:12:07Z] ERROR auth: token validation failed: KMS.Decrypt returned AccessDeniedException request-id=REQ-xxxx"
  "[2025-03-02T14:12:07Z] INFO network: outbound blocked to kms endpoint? connection refused"
  Customer says they use an HSM-backed key via a customer-managed KMS proxy in their VPC.

raj.iv (infra-eng): if the bastion can reach the control plane but app pods can't, common causes:
  - egress rules on the pod subnet block 443 to control plane / KMS endpoints
  - missing NAT gateway or misconfigured route table for private subnets
  - firewall appliance doing TLS inspection and breaking SNI
  Commands to run inside their pod (ask customer to run):
    kubectl exec -it <pod> -- curl -vk https://control-plane.internal.redwood/health
    kubectl exec -it <pod> -- openssl s_client -connect kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com:443 -servername kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
    tcpdump -nni eth0 port 443 -c 50

samir.s: also check for VPC endpoints for KMS. If they're using an endpoint, route tables must include it and security groups must allow the ENI traffic. For an HSM-backed key via proxy, ensure the proxy's SG allows egress to the KMS service and to our control plane IPs. Ask Support to share the customer's route table and SG entries (sanitized).

morgan.h: customer ran the openssl test from pod: "connect: Connection timed out". From bastion the openssl succeeds. They pasted a snippet from their firewall appliance showing a rule applied at 14:10 that drops outbound 443 to 52.xxx.xxx.xxx/32 (we suspect that's a control-plane IP).

audit-bot: NOTE — current audit retention for hosted control plane events is 7d for standard accounts; enterprise customers can request longer retention via export. Customer expects 30d retention; we need to surface that in the compliance response.

samir.s: two parallel asks:
  1) infra: confirm whether their firewall change is blocking control-plane and KMS egress from the pod CIDR.
  2) security: gather control-plane logs for the exact request-ids around the failure window to show Decrypt attempts (or absence) to the customer.

infra-eng: temporary mitigation we can instruct customer to try (low-friction):
  - allow outbound 443 from pod CIDR to control-plane CIDR and kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com (or KMS VPC endpoint ENI IPs)
  - if they have a TLS inspection appliance, bypass inspection for SNI "kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com" and control-plane hostnames
  - verify NAT gateway is present for private subnets; if missing, add a NAT or configure egress-only internet gateway
  Example iptables allow rule (customer-side):
    iptables -I OUTPUT -d 52.XX.XX.XX/32 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

morgan.h: customer opened egress to control-plane CIDR and re-ran the app request — result: 200. They then closed it again to reproduce and got 401. Once opened, control-plane logs show KMS.Decrypt request-id=REQ-abc123 with status=OK. So root cause looks like firewall/egress blocking Decrypt calls from pods to the KMS proxy/endpoint.

samir.s: good repro. Two follow-ups before closing:
  - provide customer a security-safe artifact proving Decrypt requests (control-plane log slice + request-id and timestamp). Confirm whether our audit logs contain the Decrypt event for their key; if not, explain retention and offer export.
  - add a short runbook for customers using customer-managed KMS/HSM: required egress ranges (control-plane + KMS endpoints), recommended SNIs to bypass for TLS inspection, and a NAT check.

morgan.h: also flagged compliance ask: customer requires 30d audit retention. Options:
  - export audit logs to their S3 (we can wire up an export; security/compliance to own the design)
  - provide an enterprise retention add-on (sales + billing).

infra-eng: opened an internal ticket to add the control-plane CIDR and KMS endpoint ranges to the onboarding doc and the VPC checklist. PR will include sample iptables and terraform sg rules.

samir.s: I'll draft the customer-facing summary: cause=egress/firewall blocked Decrypt calls from pod to KMS proxy, effect=control-plane couldn't validate tokens -> 401, mitigation=allow egress to control-plane and KMS endpoints, verification=we observed KMS.Decrypt request-id=REQ-abc123 succeed after rule change. Also include next steps for audit retention.

morgan.h: assigning follow-ups: #1234 (infra) update onboarding checklist, #1235 (security) prepare compliance response and audit export option, #1236 (support) confirm closure with customer after export options are presented.

support-bot: Customer updated support case: "Thanks, opening egress fixed it — please send steps so we can update our IaC." Customer requested a copy of Decrypt logs for 14 Feb -> 16 Feb. We will offer export and SLA for providing artifacts.

samir.s: closing notes — remind infra that TLS interception appliances are a common silent failure mode for HSM/KMS traffic; add a short blurb in onboarding RFC. :thumbsup:

morgan.h: thanks team. I'll follow up with the exported logs and copy of the runbook.
